# Test fixtures

## `bbsi-work-summary-payroll.xlsx`

The vendor's real daily payroll export, structurally intact, with the data
replaced.

### Why this file exists

`xlsx-lite.js` shipped with twenty passing tests and then failed on the very
first real BBSI attachment with `This .xlsx contains no worksheets`. The tests
passed because every fixture was generated by code that shared the parser's
assumptions, and a generated fixture cannot falsify an assumption its own
generator also makes.

This fixture is therefore **not generated**. It was derived from an actual
`Work Summary Payroll.xlsx` (received 2026-08-20) by copying the ZIP container
and every XML part byte-for-byte and rewriting only the cell *contents*. Every
structural property is copied rather than re-derived — including any nobody has
noticed yet. That is the whole point: do not regenerate this file from a
description of it.

### The vendor traits it pins

Six ways this differs from what Excel and openpyxl emit. The first four were
diagnosed from the failing attachment; the last two were found by inspecting
the container and were not in any description of the file.

| # | Trait | Why a parser trips on it |
|---|-------|--------------------------|
| 1 | Every element carries a namespace prefix (`<x:worksheet>`, `<x:row>`, `<x:c>`) | Matching `<sheet ` or `</si>` literally finds nothing. The prefix is the writer's choice, so match on **local name**. |
| 2 | The worksheet part is `xl/worksheets/sheet.xml` — singular, no numeric suffix | Anything guessing `sheet1.xml` misses it. The path comes from the rels. |
| 3 | Every XML part begins with a UTF-8 BOM (`EF BB BF`) | Must be stripped, not smuggled into the first header or value. |
| 4 | Rels `Target` is an absolute package path (`/xl/worksheets/sheet.xml`) | Resolution has to handle the leading slash as well as relative and `./` forms. |
| 5 | **`_rels/.rels` is STORED, not deflated** | `inflateRawSync` on every entry throws. Honour the per-entry compression method. |
| 6 | **Local headers carry a 28-byte `0xA220` extra field; the central directory reports `extra=0`** | Computing the data offset from the *central directory's* extra length lands 28 bytes short and reads garbage. Read each local header's own extra length. |

Also present, and also unlike Excel: `t="n"` is written explicitly on numeric
cells (Excel omits it, since `n` is the default); `xmlns:r` is declared on the
`<x:sheet>` element rather than the root; and `Emp #` is a *shared string*, so
`"0417"` keeps its leading zero and must not become the number 417.

### What was changed

Only cell values. Names are invented; employee numbers, pay rates, hours and
earnings are synthetic. No real name, and no real (pay rate, earnings) pair,
survives — the test asserts the shape, never a real person's pay.

Real characteristics that *are* preserved, because they drive behaviour:

- 61 data rows, 9 columns, sheet named `Work Summary Payroll`
- all 7 salaried rows come through as **all zeros** — the vendor reports no
  rate and no hours for salaried people at all, which is why the BBSI flow
  skips them unconditionally rather than reading a rate for them
- one hourly row carries a **pay rate of 0**
- one employee number keeps a **leading zero** (`0417`)
- `Regular + OT == Total Hours`, and earnings follow the 4x10 tier maths

### If you need to refresh it

Re-derive it from a new attachment the same way — copy the container, replace
the values. Do not rebuild it with a generator, and do not "clean up" a quirk
in the table above: each one is a bug this parser already had.
